author: WaveWaveYT_
quote:
I’m writing this review because I love the entire series, and I don’t want to see the game die due to decisions that are being presented as "good." 
First of all, the story is boring; the most important elements, the characters, lack any life. Take the main characters: Lucia completely dominates Jason, and it shows, Jason barely opens his mouth to speak, and he has absolutely no vitality or emotion. It’s incredibly difficult to build any rapport or narrative between just these two characters. Rockstar tried, but it’s clear they didn’t succeed. The supporting characters lack any distinct personality; sure, they exist and go about their business, but that’s about it. The mechanics are interesting, but we expected more, for instance, that infamous bit where a bottle just suddenly appears in a character's hand. We didn’t ask for an "honor" system, and there’s no logical reason for it to be included; it feels forced and restrictive, it’s not as if I’m just going around hitting people over the head. From what I understand, the game supports the LGBT community, a deplorable move for Rockstar. Don’t get me wrong, I have nothing against the people themselves, but Rockstar, with their history of edgy, often over-the-top humor, just isn't the type of company for this. Also, I don’t get why there’s hate directed toward the "furry" community when it’s essentially the same thing as the LGBT community, it makes no sense to me. You can’t have any romantic interest other than Lucia; it feels forced and illogical. There are countless other reasons, but I can’t cover them all here.  To explain my perspective, here is a comparison between GTA 6 and other Rockstar games.
 In GTA 4, the protagonist is from Yugoslavia, and it really shows; he has the temperament of an avenger, quick to start a fight and the type of person who doesn't get along with his cousin. In RDR 2, we have Arthur Morgan, a remarkably well-crafted and cohesive character with a compelling backstory; he starts off as an immovable force, only to eventually crumble under the pressure of his circumstances. It’s a deeply moving experience, you aren't forced into a single path, and the "honor" system is central to the game; it matters immensely, which is why "redemption" is in the title. 
GTA 5 features three characters, offering a wider range of possibilities. Franklin comes from the streets, he’s right at the heart of the criminal world, a reality you can truly see and feel. 
Michael is a man who has stepped back from that life; he’s a family man struggling with personal issues and communication, a fallen figure who, at times, just completely gives up on life. 
Then there’s Trevor, who makes the story truly entertaining, he’s a man who fights everyone and embodies the very definition of "GTA-style" insanity.
 In GTA: San Andreas, we have CJ, a Black protagonist living amidst gang life; it’s fascinating to get a glimpse into that world and all its associated chaos. A common thread across these games is that the first mission usually involves stealing something, a car or some other vehicle. In GTA 6, by contrast, the opening missions involve... cleaning up a house. The "honor" system feels completely out of place here.
 In GTA 5, the characters were forced to steal just to survive, and from there, everything spiraled out of control.  Lucia wants to steal just for the sake of having things, a pathetic story.
 If I’m to be silenced for my own opinions, and if I’ve offended anyone with my previous remarks, I apologie, well, I’ve loved this series since I was 8 years old, back when I didn’t even know what I was doing on that computer, all the way back to GTA III. 
You can find more information online about how the trailer doesn’t align with the actual game, why the game is capped at 30 fps, and so on; I know all of it, but I’m not going to cover every single point. It’s just sad... I hate that I have to witness this.
